verdict.root_cause: productcatalogservice is returning application-level gRPC status 13 INTERNAL on its GetProduct operation because a deliberate "ProductCatalogService failure" feature flag is enabled. Frontend's client-side gRPC errors name that flag explicitly in the status detail (tr_aaee60f94860), and the trace topology corroborates the mechanism structurally: every failing GetProduct span carries an accompanying FeatureFlagService/GetFlag lookup that no successful GetProduct span in the sample shows, and the innermost ERROR sits on the productcatalogservice server span itself rather than on any downstream (tr_3eb0d8be9dd7). The failure is fast-returning, not slow — failing spans finish in 0.8–2.7ms versus sub-0.1ms for successes — so nothing is waiting on or starving for a resource. Impact fans out from there: frontend browse paths and the checkout path both fail through the same catalog dependency, with checkout aborting at the catalog lookup before currency/shipping/payment/email run (tr_3eb0d8be9dd7, tr_aaee60f94860). Error ratios are partial and bursty rather than total — ~10.7% at productcatalogservice and ~9.4% at frontend, both touching zero within the window (tr_1e5fc3db1c61, tr_713acf69c44d) — consistent with a flag that fails a fraction of lookups rather than all of them. The flag's enablement is the wrong value and the wrong value is what breaks each request, so the fix is to turn it off, not to roll back or restart anything.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent lines converge on the same mechanism. The frontend log evidence (tr_aaee60f94860) gives a direct, self-describing attribution: gRPC code 13 INTERNAL with detail text naming an enabled ProductCatalogService failure flag, arriving via grpc-js callErrorFromStatus — i.e. frontend is relaying a status the downstream produced, not generating one. The trace evidence (tr_3eb0d8be9dd7) independently isolates the same locus without relying on the message text: the innermost ERROR is the productcatalogservice server span, failures appear under multiple distinct callers (frontend GET, checkout PlaceOrder, and an orphan root), only GetProduct is affected while ListProducts succeeds in the same traces, and the one structural feature separating failing from succeeding GetProduct spans is the GetFlag lookup. Competing classes are excluded by the specialists' own rule-outs rather than by assumption: resource_exhaustion is inconsistent with sub-3ms failing spans, sub-millisecond concurrent successes, and the absence of RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED/429/503 codes (tr_3eb0d8be9dd7, tr_aaee60f94860); dependency_latency is excluded because no downstream service span carries ERROR, the cart lookup succeeds before the catalog call fails, and the extra time is single-digit milliseconds with no deadline signature (tr_3eb0d8be9dd7); bad_deploy is unsupported because no deploy or rollout record exists in the onset window and frontend is faithfully surfacing a downstream status rather than misbehaving itself (tr_7acd7d63b739, tr_aaee60f94860). The change-history dispatches came back empty (tr_0e11de1a36c2, tr_7acd7d63b739), but both specialists flagged that they only covered 17:56–18:11 of a requested two-hour window, so an earlier flag toggle is unexcluded rather than disproven — the empty change log therefore neither supports nor contradicts the verdict. The productcatalogservice log dispatch returned nothing at all under a mismatched label selector (tr_c50e39c0e75e), so the service's own account of the failure was never actually retrieved; I treat that as a gap, not as silence. Classification rests on what the service is doing wrong now: it is deliberately returning INTERNAL because a flag says to, and clearing the flag stops it — the misconfiguration is the mechanism, not merely an act upstream of it.
open_questions: When and by whom the failure flag was enabled is unestablished — roughly 110 minutes (16:06–17:56) of change history were never queried, and no toggle record exists in the 15 minutes that were. Onset at 18:06:15 with frontend errors already visible at ~18:02:57 suggests the toggle predates the page.

Why the error ratio is partial and bursty (~10%, dipping to zero) rather than total: whether the flag fails a probability-weighted fraction of lookups, applies to a subset of product IDs, or is set on only some replicas. Nothing dispatched distinguishes these.

productcatalogservice's own logs were never actually read — the Loki selector used 'product-catalog-service' against a service named 'productcatalogservice' and returned zero lines of any severity. The service's first-person account of the flag evaluation should be re-queried against the correct label before this is considered closed.
Which HTTP routes and what share of user sessions are affected is unknown: the frontend metric carries no route dimension and the frontend log result contains no HTTP request lines.
The unmeasured edge crossed in triage was never resolved to a specific service pair, so blast radius beyond the seven named services is not fully bounded.
Whether checkout failures produced partial or abandoned orders needing cleanup — traces show the order pipeline absent after the catalog abort, but no dispatch examined order state.
Whether this flag is a leftover from an intentional fault-injection or chaos exercise, which would change the remediation owner even though it does not change the technical fix.
